title: Vendor accreditation & billing pathways kickoff - Aurora FinReg
summary: Kickoff to align on vendor accreditation (MSA/DPA), billing approval path, pricing tiers, and preliminary technical checklist for private deployment options. Action items include security docs share, pricing scenarios to finance, and draft MSA redlines from Aurora legal.
topics: Private vs hosted deployment tradeoffs and KMS/SSO requirements
action_items: Priya Menon - send Aurora MSA redline summary - Due: 2026-05-28
Ethan Rodriguez - provide Dedicated capacity throughput profile & benchmark spreadsheet - Due: 2026-05-25
Leila Cho - share standard MSA and DPA + SOC2 package links - Due: 2026-05-23
Robert Mills - confirm internal pricing approver list and cadence - Due: 2026-05-29
next_steps: Redwood to upload security bundle (SOC2, encryption whitepaper, pen test) to sharepoint
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) for platform integration next week
Finance-to-finance pricing review meeting to be scheduled by Aurora
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-21 15:32 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Rodriguez (Redwood SE), Leila Cho (Redwood Legal Ops); Sanjay Rao (Aurora Procurement), Hannah Li (Aurora InfoSec), Robert Mills (Aurora Finance), Priya Menon (Aurora Legal), Tom Vega (Aurora Platform)
transcript:
00:00 - Maya Patel: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. um we wanted to make this kickoff a quick alignment on the accreditation path and, uh, who needs what to get through Aurora's vendor committee.
00:12 - Sanjay Rao: great thanks Maya. yeah we have a few blockers on, like, two fronts: legal redlines (MSA/DPA) and then finance approval for committed spends. also curious about private deployment options for regulated workloads.
00:27 - Maya Patel: totally — we can cover those. quick intros then we'll go into the workbook. i'm Maya, AE. ethan's our technical lead and Leila handles the legal ops side for redlines.
00:40 - Ethan Rodriguez: hey all, quick note on the Dedicated capacity we discussed — it's reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput. i'll show numbers later in the benchmark sheet.
00:51 - Hannah Li: hi, hannah here from infosec — primary questions: where is data at rest, what KMS options, and do you provide audit logs and long-term retention?
01:03 - Leila Cho: we have a standard KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and HSM options for private. SOC2 Type II report and pen test available, i will share.
01:12 - Priya Menon: on the MSA, we typically see vendor clauses around data residency and liability caps as sticking points. do you accept custom cap language or is it fixed?
01:23 - Maya Patel: we do have standard caps but enterprise customers often negotiate — it's a case-by-case. leila will pull the typical redline playbook.
01:31 - Tom Vega: from platform's perspective, latency SLOs are important. if we go hosted, what are realistic p50/p95 numbers for 8k context?
01:42 - Ethan Rodriguez: for our hosted API, p50 is usually sub-80ms for short responses; p95 depends on token length and model. for Dedicated, we can guarantee tighter SLOs and throughput at committed tiers. technical deep-dive will give the exact numbers.
01:55 - Robert Mills: on the billing path — our procurement needs a pricing approver chain and the commit language for reserved capacity. what does Redwood require for minimum commitment?
02:08 - Maya Patel: we have monthly and annual reserved capacity contracts; minimums vary by region and config. we can present three pricing scenarios: pay-as-you-go, 3-month pilot reserved, and 12-month committed capacity.
02:20 - Sanjay Rao: okay can you put that in a simple finance spreadsheet? our pricing committee needs per-token numbers and uplift for SLA/priority.
02:29 - Ethan Rodriguez: yes i'll add per-token estimates and an uplift matrix for higher SLA tiers. i'll also include cache/batching assumptions because those materially affect unit cost.
02:40 - Hannah Li: about the DPA — do you support EU data residency and specific subprocessors list?
02:48 - Leila Cho: yes we support EU residency, and subprocessors list is in the security bundle. we can add contract language for subprocessors if needed.
02:56 - Priya Menon: timeline wise, how long does vendor committee take once docs are provided? we need to put milestones on the calendar.
03:04 - Sanjay Rao: typically 3-6 weeks internal review if there are moderate redlines; finance adds another week.
03:09 - Maya Patel: understood — our plan: share MSA/DPA + SOC2 today, you review, priya sends redlines, then legal sync.
03:17 - Tom Vega: technical integration question — if we choose Private VPC, do you provision a customer-managed control plane or is it fully on-prem?
03:26 - Ethan Rodriguez: for Private we do a customer-controlled plane with an appliance option for air-gapped customers. networking is customer-managed — we provide deployment docs and an ops runbook.
03:36 - Sanjay Rao: what about entitlements and RBAC? we need SSO (SAML/SCIM) and enterprise RBAC.
03:44 - Leila Cho: SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning is supported; RBAC roles are customizable and we can map to Aurora groups.
03:52 - Robert Mills: can you explain billing reconciliation for reserved capacity? we need invoice granularity and usage breakdowns for showback.
04:01 - Maya Patel: invoices include per-route token breakdown, committed vs overage, and line items for dedicated pools — all visible in the Redwood Console.
04:10 - Priya Menon: legal will want indemnity and breach notification timelines spelled out; also DOJ style requests — do you have a law enforcement disclosure policy?
04:19 - Leila Cho: yes we have a standard law-enforcement disclosure clause, and breach notification SLA aligned to industry norms; we'll include that in the DPA appendix.
04:28 - Sanjay Rao: can we talk about escalation path? our vendor ops need a named contact and on-call for production incidents.
04:34 - Maya Patel: absolutely — enterprise contracts include support SLAs, named technical account manager (TAM) and 24/7 escalation for P1s depending on the support tier.
04:44 - Hannah Li: another security point: do you support customer-uploaded models or is inference only on your model catalog?
04:52 - Ethan Rodriguez: on Dedicated and Private, you can bring your own model artifacts; hosted catalog is curated. bringing your own model has additional security checklist but fully supported.
05:03 - Sanjay Rao: that's important for us — some regulated workflows use internally trained models. we'll need a guardrail document.
05:09 - Maya Patel: noted, we'll include a BYO-model security checklist.
05:14 - Robert Mills: pricing — what kind of discounts for multi-region reserved capacity?
05:21 - Maya Patel: multi-region commitments can be packaged with an enterprise discount; finance will need to see committed spend numbers to approve.
05:28 - Priya Menon: can you confirm where we can find your SOC2 cert and the pen test summary?
05:33 - Leila Cho: i'll drop links in the follow-up, plus a short summary of remediation items from the last pen test.
05:40 - Tom Vega: we also need to validate egress costs, data transfer — who bears that?
05:46 - Maya Patel: typically egress is charged per cloud region usage; for Private we can negotiate different terms. we'll document egress assumptions in the pricing workbook.
05:56 - Sanjay Rao: ok good. let's outline a milestone plan now so procurement can slot approvals.
06:02 - Maya Patel: proposed milestones: Day 0 — security bundle and pricing scenarios shared; Day 3 — Aurora sends MSA redlines; Day 10 — Redwood responds to redlines; Day 20 — pricing committee meeting; Day 28 — anticipated procurement sign-off.
06:18 - Sanjay Rao: sounds reasonable, though i'd add a buffer for finance review.
06:23 - Robert Mills: yes pls add one week buffer before final sign-off.
06:28 - Maya Patel: will do. moving on to specific document asks — priya, what format do you prefer for redlines?
06:33 - Priya Menon: Word redline is preferred, plus a one-pager summarizing significant legal exceptions.
06:38 - Leila Cho: we'll prepare a redline template to speed reviews.
06:42 - Ethan Rodriguez: technical deliverable list i'll send: benchmark spreadsheet, network diagram, ops runbook, and BYO-model checklist.
06:50 - Hannah Li: regarding KMS, do you support BYOK and rotation policies?
06:56 - Leila Cho: yes, BYOK supported; rotation policies documented.
07:01 - Tom Vega: is there an escrow or data escrow option if we terminate?
07:07 - Maya Patel: we have data export and retention terms; escrow is negotiable for large enterprise deals, we'll flag with legal.
07:14 - Sanjay Rao: any open-source licensing risk we should be aware of?
07:18 - Ethan Rodriguez: we publish dependencies and licenses; we'll include a software bill of materials (SBOM) in the security bundle.
07:26 - Priya Menon: how do you handle third-party subprocessors in the DPA, i.e. notification for changes?
07:32 - Leila Cho: subprocessors list is in the DPA; material changes trigger notice and, in some cases, the right to object.
07:39 - Robert Mills: can you give an example of a typical SLA in a Dedicated contract?
07:44 - Ethan Rodriguez: example: 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools, with latency targets per model; credits for P1/P2 SLA misses. dispute resolution and uptime measurement in Console.
07:57 - Sanjay Rao: for pricing committee, we'll need worst-case overage scenario and mitigation steps — how does Redwood cap overages?
08:06 - Maya Patel: you can cap overage charges with alerts and throttles; we can structure hard caps in contracts but typically it's monitored with automatic notifications.
08:18 - Priya Menon: regarding liability, are you able to accept Aurora's proposed carve-outs for regulated data?
08:26 - Leila Cho: we'll need to review specifics but we can often agree to stricter data residency and handling clauses; liability caps still likely to be a negotiation point.
08:36 - Tom Vega: integration tech Q: do you provide a staging environment that mirrors production infra for acceptance testing?
08:42 - Ethan Rodriguez: yes we provide a staging cluster and test harness for performance tests. we can also run dedicated benchmark runs with your sample prompts.
08:52 - Maya Patel: action items recap — leila shares security bundle today; ethan provides benchmark & pricing workbook; priya sends redlines; robert confirms approver list.
09:03 - Sanjay Rao: good. one process note — Aurora's legal board meets Wednesdays, so if we can get the redline by Monday that would help.
09:11 - Maya Patel: we'll target Monday for redline response.
09:15 - Hannah Li: last q from me — do you do background checks on your staff that have access to customer data?
09:21 - Leila Cho: standard background checks for employees with production access; specifics in the security bundle.
09:27 - Robert Mills: finance will also need sample invoices.
09:31 - Maya Patel: we'll include sample invoice templates in the follow-up packet.
09:36 - Priya Menon: timeline request: can we aim to get to a signed MSA by the end of June?
09:41 - Sanjay Rao: end of June would be tight but possible if redlines are light.
09:47 - Maya Patel: we'll work to meet that. ok any other items?
09:50 - Tom Vega: maybe just to reiterate: network egress, deployment diagram, and SSO flow.
09:55 - Ethan Rodriguez: i'll include diagrams and a step-by-step SAML/SCIM guide.
10:01 - Maya Patel: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the bundle and proposed milestone calendar. meeting adjourned.
52:00 - [END]
